newsitem.title: UK: Turkey debut lira Eurobond due this week.
newsitem.headline: Turkey debut lira Eurobond due this week.

text.p: Turkey will issue its expected lira Eurobond this week, an official at lead manager Chase said on Monday.
"Turkey held investor presentations in Italy last Thursday and Friday which were well-attended," a syndicate manager at Chase told Reuters.
"Turkey will be the first non-Latin American emerging market borrower in the lira sector, and therefore has rarity appeal," he said.
The deal would have a five-year maturity but the size had not yet been decided, the Chase official said. Dealers elsewhere said a bond of around 300 billion lire was expected.
In January, Moody's Investors Service said it was considering cutting Turkey's Ba3 long-term foreign currency debt rating. Turkey is rated B by Standard & Poor's.
A Turkish minister said last week Moody's was unlikely to downgrade the country's foreign debt.

Turkey successfully raised 500 million marks in January. Dealers said it was easier for Turkey to raise funds in marks than in other currencies because of the large amounts of expatriate Turkish funds in Germany.
"The Turkish contingent in Germany always allows it to tap the mark sector aggressively," an emerging markets trader at a U.S. bank said.
"It is not as easy to sell Turkey in other currencies."
The lira deal was first mooted for 500 billion lire, but the country was likely to issue a smaller transaction, traders said.
